## IRouteForcedReply type

Route atom: forced reply for a method whose ONLY route is a send.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type IRouteForcedReply = INeverFields<`editOptions` | `fallbackOptions` | `fallback`> & {
    mode?: `reply`;
    keyboard?: IInBoKb | null;
    rich?: IOptReplyRich[0] | null;
    richOptions?: IOptRichSend | null;
    options?: IOptReply | null;
    broadcast?: null | undefined;
    chunkSize?: null | undefined;
};
```
**References:** [INeverFields](./gramstax.ineverfields.md)<!-- -->, [IInBoKb](./gramstax.iinbokb.md)<!-- -->, [IOptReplyRich](./gramstax.ioptreplyrich.md)<!-- -->, [IOptRichSend](./gramstax.ioptrichsend.md)<!-- -->, [IOptReply](./gramstax.ioptreply.md)

## Remarks

Identical to [IRouteReply](./gramstax.iroutereply.md) except that `mode` is optional. On a method with a single route there is nothing for `mode` to discriminate, so requiring it would force every call site to write a value that carries no information — `renderDice({mode: 'reply'})` says nothing the method name has not already said. `mode` stays in the key set and keeps its single legal value, so an explicit `mode: 'reply'` is still accepted and anything else is a compile error.
